question: Who hears consumer complaints and where can I appeal the decision?
reference_answer: Per province. Punjab: a District Judge or Additional District Judge designated by the Lahore High Court as Consumer Court; appeal to the Lahore High Court within 30 days. Sindh: a Consumer Court presided over by a Judicial Magistrate; appeal to the District and Sessions Court within 30 days.
answer: Consumer complaints can be heard by the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Federal Ombudsman) who may hold personal hearings for complaints at specified dates and times. Complaints can be presented in person to the Mohtasib through the Registrar at the Head Office or Regional Office. If the complainant or the agency is dissatisfied with the decision of the Wafaqi Mohtasib, they can file a representation to the President within 30 days of receipt of the decision. The President's Secretariat Legal Wing examines such representations and gives decisions within 90 days [S1][S2].

question: Do I have to apply for my passport at the office for the address on my CNIC, or can I go to any passport office?
reference_answer: The current DGIP page quotes the revised Passport Rule 6 (2021): any citizen may apply at any passport office irrespective of the CNIC/NICOP/CRC address. The Rules PDF text says the first passport is issued by the office for the CNIC address and later ones from the office where the applicant temporarily resides, with address attestation. Both should be cited, the revised rule presented as current.
answer: According to the Revised Provisions of Passport Rule 6, 2021, every Citizen of Pakistan may apply for Passport Services from any Passport Office irrespective of their address recorded in the Computerized National Identity Card (CNIC) / National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOP) / Child Registration Certificate (CRC) [S1]. However, the first ever passport shall be issued from the passport office in whose jurisdiction the address of the applicant, present or permanent, as recorded on the CNIC, falls. Subsequent passports may be issued from any passport office where the applicant is temporarily residing, subject to attestation of present address by a gazetted officer [S2]. There are exemptions for government or semi-government servants, armed forces personnel, employees of autonomous bodies, corporations or statutory authorities and their dependent family members at the place of posting; bonafide students of an educational institution from the passport office in whose jurisdiction that institute falls; and any person exempted by the zonal head for reasons to be recorded in writing [S2].
citations: [S1] PP-01__general-requirements-for-passport-documents-renewal-lost-pri.html p.None: Every Citizen of Pakistan may apply for Passport Services from any Passport Office irrespective of their address recorded in the Computerized National Identity Card (CNIC) / National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOP) / Child Registration Certificate (CRC). | [S2] PP-03__passport-rules-2021-sro-245-i-2022.pdf p.3: The first ever passport shall be issued from the passport office in whose jurisdiction the address of the applicant, present or permanent, as recorded on the Computerized National Identity Card (CNIC), falls. The subsequent passports may be issued from any passport office, under jurisdiction whereof the applicant is temporarily residing, subject to attestation of present address by a gazetted officer. However, persons falling under the following categories are exempted from this provision, namely:- (a) Government or semi-government servants, armed forces personnel, employees of autonomous bodies, corporations or statutory authorities and their dependent family members at the place of posting; (b) bonafide student of an educational institution, from the passport office in whose jurisdiction that institute falls; and (c) any person exempted by the zonal head for reasons to be recorded in writing.

question: When is the Active Taxpayer List published, and what surcharge does a company pay to be added after the due date?
reference_answer: (1) Every year on 1 March. (2) PKR 20,000 for a company.
answer: The Active Taxpayer List (ATL) is published every financial year on the 1st of March and is valid up to the last day of February of the next financial year. For example, the ATL for the tax year 2020 was published on 1st March 2021 and valid till 28th February 2022. Similarly, the ATL for the tax year 2021 was published on 1st March 2022 and valid till 28th February 2023. The ATL is updated every Monday on the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) website. A company that files its tax return after the due date can still be included in the ATL by paying a surcharge of one hundred thousand rupees to be added after the due date of filing the tax return.

question: In Sindh, where do appeals against a consumer court order go?
reference_answer: To the District and Sessions Court, within 30 days. The 2023 amendment replaced 'Sindh High Court' with 'District and Sessions Court'; the original 2015 text said the Sindh High Court.
answer: In Sindh, any person aggrieved by a final order of the Consumer Court may file an appeal in the Sindh High Court within 30 days of such order. The appeal must be filed in accordance with the Rules of Procedure of the Sindh High Court and accompanied by a memorandum of appeal along with the certified copy of the order of the Court appealed against and supporting documents. If the appeal is presented after the expiry of the 30-day period, an application explaining sufficient cause for the delay must be included. The Sindh High Court may exercise all or any of the powers of the Consumer Court in respect of the appeal pending before it [S3][S4].

question: If my complaint is not on WMS Form A, what must it include?
reference_answer: A solemn affirmation that the allegations are true; no previous complaint on the subject was filed; no court, tribunal or board proceedings are pending; and a representation to the agency was made but not answered in reasonable time or unjustly turned down.
answer: If a complaint is not lodged on WMS-Form 'A', it shall be accompanied by a solemn affirmation that: (a) the allegations contained in the complaint are correct and true to the best of knowledge and belief of the complainant; (b) previously no complaint on the subject was filed at the Head Office or any of the Regional Offices; (c) no suit, appeal, petition or any other judicial proceedings in connection with the subject matter of the complaint is pending before any Court, Tribunal or Board; and (d) a representation to a competent authority of the Agency in respect of the allegations contained in the complaint was made, but either no reply thereto was given within a reasonable time or the representation had unjustly been turned down [S1][S3].

question: کیا وفاقی محتسب میں شکایت درج کرانے کی کوئی فیس ہے؟
reference_answer: No fee is charged and no lawyer is needed; the complainant can plead the case personally.
answer: وفاقی محتسب میں شکایت درج کرانے کی کوئی فیس نہیں ہے اور نہ ہی کسی وکیل کی ضرورت ہے۔ شکایت کنندہ اپنے کیس کی خود ہی پیروی کر سکتا ہے۔[S1][S2]
citations: [S1] RC-02__wafaqi-mohtasib-faqs-about-complaints.html p.None: وفاقی محتسب میں شکا یت درج کرا نے کی کو ئی فیس نہیں اور نہ ہی کسی وکیل کی ضرورت ہے۔ شکا یت کنند ہ اپنے کیس کی خودہی پیر وی کر سکتا ہے۔ | [S2] RC-02__wafaqi-mohtasib-faqs-about-complaints.html p.None: No fee is charged for filing a complaint. There is no requirement to engage a lawyer as the complainant can plead the case personally.

question: I am an overseas Pakistani. What do I need to change my name on my NICOP or CNIC?
reference_answer: Apply through the mobile app with an S1 form issued by the Pakistan Embassy/Mission, or a notarized/attested name-change deed, or an undertaking attested by the Embassy/Mission; AND a Pakistani/foreign passport, residence permit, work permit, travel document, or Undertaking 'A' attested by the Pakistan Embassy/Mission.
answer: To change your name on your CNIC or NICOP as an overseas Pakistani, you need to submit a notarized declaration affirming the name change, stating the old and new names and the reason for the change, and confirming that you will update your educational and other documents accordingly. This declaration must be signed and dated by you, and includes your CNIC/NICOP number and residence details [S3]. Additionally, you must provide a declaration stating that you have changed your name while acquiring nationality of another country, mentioning the new name as per your foreign passport, attaching a copy of the name change deed if it is a full name change. This declaration must be signed, dated, witnessed, and notarized [S4].

question: Agar main return late file karun to ATL mein aane ke liye individual ko kitna surcharge dena hoga?
reference_answer: Rs 1,000 for individuals (AOP Rs 10,000, company Rs 20,000), under the Finance Act 2019 rule that late filers can still be placed on the ATL.
answer: Agar aap individual hain aur late tax return file karte hain to ATL mein shamil hone ke liye aapko 25,000 rupees ka surcharge dena hoga[S2][S3].
citations: [S2] TX-04__income-tax-ordinance-2001-amended-up-to-30-06-2026.pdf p.428: (iii) 1[twenty-five] thousand in case of an individual. | [S3] TX-02b__active-taxpayer-list-what-it-is-inclusion-how-to-check-statu.html p.None: The late filers of Income Tax Return for Tax Year 2021 can pay “Surcharge for ATL” as defined under section 182(A) of Income Tax Ordinance 2001 by clicking on Tax Payment Nature “Misc” head in the PSID.

question: شناختی کارڈ پر تاریخ پیدائش پانچ سال سے زیادہ بدلنی ہو تو کیا چاہیے؟
reference_answer: Any one of the documents accepted for a change of up to 5 years (e.g. a verified computerized birth certificate, matric/equivalent certificate, valid passport, verified government service record) plus approval from DG Ops / HOD IOOD or the regional DG. A change of 10 or more years is processed only with DG approval and a justification.
